blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Samson was the strongest man in Israel. Before he was born, God had set him apart. No razor was ever to touch his head. His long hair was the sign of that promise. For years he fought the Philistines, who ruled over Israel.

verses.text: And it came to pass afterward, that he loved a woman in the valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah.

verses.text: And the lords of the Philistines came up unto her, and said unto her, Entice him, and see wherein his great strength lieth, and by what means we may prevail against him, that we may bind him to afflict him: and we will give thee every one of us eleven hundred pieces of silver.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Eleven hundred pieces of silver from each of the lords. It was a fortune, and Delilah said yes.

verses.text: And Delilah said to Samson, Tell me, I pray thee, wherein thy great strength lieth, and wherewith thou mightest be bound to afflict thee.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Samson played a game with her. He told her to bind him with fresh bowstrings, and he snapped them. He told her new ropes, and he broke those like thread. He told her to weave his hair into a loom, and he walked away with the whole thing. Each time, the Philistines were waiting in the room. Each time, Samson should have seen what was happening.

verses.text: And she said unto him, How canst thou say, I love thee, when thine heart is not with me? thou hast mocked me these three times, and hast not told me wherein thy great strength lieth.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: That is one of the saddest lines in the Bible. Samson thought he would get up and shake himself free like before. He did not know that the LORD had left him.

verses.text: But the Philistines took him, and put out his eyes, and brought him down to Gaza, and bound him with fetters of brass; and he did grind in the prison house.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The strongest man in Israel, blind and in chains, pushing a grinding stone in a prison. Everything he had been was gone.

verses.text: Howbeit the hair of his head began to grow again after he was shaven.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: But the story does not stop there. A small line, easy to miss. His hair began to grow again.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The Philistines held a great feast to thank their god for giving them Samson. They brought him out of the prison to make fun of him, and stood him between the pillars of the temple. Thousands of people were watching.

verses.text: And Samson said unto the lad that held him by the hand, Suffer me that I may feel the pillars whereupon the house standeth, that I may lean upon them.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: For the first time in this story, Samson asked God for help. Not for a game or for pride. He prayed, remember me.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Samson's life was full of choices he should not have made. The Bible does not hide them. But at the very end, broken and blind, he called on God, and God heard him. Samson is listed later among the people of faith in the book of Hebrews. Not because he got everything right, but because at the last he turned to God and asked to be remembered.
